question_text: Read the passage on the Nobel Prize. Complete the following table with information from
stimulus: the passage. 15=5 The Nobel Prize is the world's most prestigious and important prize. This award has been given since 1901. Generaly, it is given to persons who have outstanding contributions to Physics, Chemistry, Literature, Medicine (Physiology), Peace and Economics. Economics was added to the list in 1969 for the first time. The Nobel Prize was instituted by the inventor of dynamite. This scientist was Alfred Bernard Nobel. He was born in Stockholm, Sweden on October 21, 1833 and died in 1896. He completed his education in Russia. He earned a huge amount of money by selling dynamite. At the time of his death in 1896, Nobel left behind this huge amount of money. He also left a will indicating that the interest on his money should be given as prize to persons for their outstanding contributions to Physics, Chemistry, Literature, Medicine and Peace. The prize was named Nobel Prize. The first Nobel Prize was given to Rontgen on December 10, 1901 for inventing X-rays. Name of the Events Place Year/ Time Achievement Alfred Nobel was born (i) — 1833 Nobel Prize was launched (ii) — Economics was added to the list (iii) — Alfred completed education (iv) — First time, Nobel Prize was given 1901 (v) —

stimulus: the passage. 15=5 Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States. He is famous for his Gettysburg Address delivered on November 19, 1863 during the American Civil War. He was a captain in the Black Hawk War. He won the Presidential nomination in 1860 and he became the President of the United States in 1861. stimulus: passage. 15=5 In 1912, an American Shipping company launched a new ship called 'The Titanic." 'It was the largest and most luxurious ocean liner of the time. It weighed 46,000 tons and could carry about 2200 passengers. Experts said that nothing could make it sink. On April 10, 1912, the ship sailed on its first voyage across the Atlantic. It sailed from Southampton in England to New York in the United States with 2224 passengers — men, women and children. On April 15, just before midnight the ship struck a large ice-berg. The ice-berg tore a great hole in the ship's side and the unsinkable 'Titanic' began to sink. There was a great alarm on board. Warning bells rang out. question_text: Read the passage on Mother Teresa. Complete the following table with information from the
stimulus: passage. 15=5 Mother Teresa is a dedicated soul like sister Nibedita. Both of them were originally foreigners, but made this region their home. Teresa was born in 1910 at Skopje, a small village in Yugoslavia. Her earlier name was Agnes. At, eighteen she decided to become a nun, so she came to India in 1928 and became an Indian citizen. Thus though she was an Albanian, she became an Indian by choice. She started her life in Kolkata as a teacher in a convent school, but soon the mother in her cried for the suffering of the poor and the downtrodden. Her "Nirmal Hriday" at Kalighat becomes the shelter of the sufferings. Her activities have now been spread all over the world. In 1979 she was awarded the Nobel Prize for peace. She was awarded 'Bharat Ratna Award" for the year 1980. It was very surprising that even at her very ripe old age she intersely did her selfless service for mankind, irrespective of caste and creed. She breathed her last on 15th September, 1997 at the age of 87. question_text: Read the passage about William Blake. Complete the following table with information from the
stimulus: passage. William Blake, a poet and artist, was born in London in 1757. During his early years, he showed himself as a dreamer and visionary. Beyond learning to read and write, he received no education but began to copy prints and write verses at the age of ten. At the age of fourteen, he was apprenticed to an engraver. He married Catherine Boucher at the age of twenty five, and shortly afterwards, set up a print shop. A patron of him provided him a cottage on the Sussex Coast. He spent all his life in London. 'The Poet Sketches', a collection of his early poems, was published in 1783. With the help of his wife, he published 'Songs of Innocence' in 1789. 'Songs of Experience' was published five years later. His only book in prose named 'The Marriage of Heaven and Hell' was published in 1790. His other book 'Milton' was written in 1804. He died at his sixty-nine years.
